id_range.rule: Minted in the existing register (N/P/F/C/S/O/W + integer, per schemas/metagraph-v1-schema.json) but from 201 upward: the store holds 1..21 and the health proposal holds 101..110, so 201+ collides with neither and is self-evidently an outcome-overlay proposal on sight. schema_note: This file does NOT validate against schemas/metagraph-v1-schema.json as written, on three points, none of which is fixed here: (1) `provenance` is an enum of ["pod-0", "method-pod"] and this file needs "outcome-overlay-mint" — the same one-line widening the health proposal needs; (2) walk steps and branch arms that are MINTED carry no `row` (the schema's row pattern ^g[0-9]+$ is a pod-0 row id and a minted turn has none) — they carry `minted: true` instead, and where the schema REQUIRES `row` on a branch arm the minted arm omits it; (3) the concept `proposed-additions` is not one of the schema's five file kinds, exactly as the health proposal. Nothing about the existing store is changed to accommodate any of this.
store_untouched: nodes.json, moves.json, edges.json, outcome-shapes.json and walks/pod-0.json are byte-identical to origin/main (bcec51c04). POD-1 is attested evidence and is extended here — every arm hangs off a fork POD-1 already has — never re-cut.

ruling_recorded.basis: Tom's ruling, U1 = YES: asking presupposes surviving a plain no, so non-delivery-with-a-reason is position 1 and the floor of the overlay.
ruling_recorded.discrepancy: outcome-shapes.json carries sequence: [O3, O1, O4, O2, O5, O6, O7, O8, O9] with O3 at sequence_position 1 and O1 at 2. The store is NOT edited to match. Nothing in the survivability edges decides between the two floors — every ask presupposes both S201 (surviving a no) and S203 (reformulating on demand); the store's array chose O3 on latency, the ruling chooses O1, and the ruling wins.
ruling_recorded.proposed_sequence_basis: O1 by ruling. O3 next because S203 is presupposed by every produced turn including O6's admission. O6 before O7 because S205 makes O6 presuppose O1 and its cost of failing to recover is the highest of the four; O7's redemption latency is 1 but its failure is invisible. Rungs: lower before higher within each shape (S202; cost). See the document §7.

nodes.why_not_an_existing_node: N3's negative alternative is F6 — the refuser supplies the substitute and the asker picks (g59→g60). N7 is F5 — the refuser supplies the counter. In both, the refuser does the asker's next move for them. N201 is the shape where they do not. That position — holding nothing and having to move — is the one the corpus never lets anyone occupy.

nodes.why_not_an_existing_node: P101 and N11 positions 1–2 are self-blame for imposing, answered by absolution — ritual fault, waved away. N203 is real fault that is not waved. nodes.gloss: Mid-business, the other party steps out of the frame unbidden and discloses worry or difficulty. The learner marks it as heard and does nothing about it; the discloser closes the aside; the business resumes.

nodes.why_not_an_existing_node: N12 is the LEARNER's trouble, answered by an elicit and a remedy (g110→g111 — the store's 'starkest absence of sympathy'). N11 positions 5–6 are a symmetric move on the learner's own difficulty. F102 is normality asserted from the knowledge seat. Nothing in the store has the native disclose and the learner receive without doing anything about it. The recovery is half a withholding, which is why it is hard to attest.
nodes.asymmetry_note: At a counter the customer's trouble gets processed — that is what a counter is for — so the customer's disclosure becomes an elicit and g110→g111 is right to write it so. The only disclosure that gets to be an aside at a counter is the one from behind it. That is K1 at work: the K1-holder processes the other's trouble. It is why W208 has the pharmacist disclose, and why the rung-0 arm cannot sit on the chemist's.
nodes.smoke_test: Passes — and it changed F204: 'does not match with a disclosure of one's own' was wrong for columns where the matched line IS the acknowledgement. What survives every column is the exclusion of fixing and of withdrawing.

walk_set.format: Same as walks/pod-0.json: a walk is a sequence of node references {step, node, position}; surface is an annotation. Each walk's stem step is an existing pod-0 row and the fork is a `branches` array on that step, one arm being the corpus's own continuation and the other the minted arm this walk follows. A fork is satisfied by any ONE arm. `minted: true` marks turns that exist nowhere in pod-0; `built_from` cites the pod-0 rows a minted turn is fused from. `learner_side` names the learner's speaker label. `rung` and `kinds_held_by_other_party` place the scene on the ladder of asymmetry (see `ladder`).

second_axis_test.result: Supported as a tie-breaker and as the register key; not as a primary key. Latency alone ties O1, O3 and O7 at 1 and puts O7 BEFORE O6 — which neither the store's order nor sense agrees with. Cost breaks the tie (O7's failure is invisible; O3's costs a drink or a ticket; O1-asym's costs the bus) and orders the rungs inside every shape, lower before higher, every time. But cost cannot be primary: if it were, W206 (the penalty) would outrank O3 entirely, and S203 says you cannot survive the inspector without first being able to reformulate on demand. So the order is: the ruling (O1 first), then survivability (S203 puts O3 next; S205 puts O6 after O1), then latency, then cost as the tie-breaker and the register key. The prediction was right on both halves.
second_axis_test.refinement_from_health_confirmed: The health mapping put the weight on the shape, not the line. Here the weight sits on the RUNG — the count and kind of asymmetry, a shape variable on the trunk — so the two findings are the same finding.
